articles.title: Want To Smell Like a Werwulf? This Perfume Has You Covered
articles.body:
Nothing says date night like the smell of "the heat of flesh that was once human." Robert Eggers' Werwulf hits movie theaters at Christmas, but you can pre-order an official perfume set based on the movie right now. Focus Features has teamed up with the very fancy Heretic Parfum for a set of three very specific fragrances.

Designed to represent each stage of a werewolf transformation, the descriptions of each of the scents are a wild ride.

The Wode Hath Teth: The scent of the feral woodland itself. Cold bark, frozen soil, and smoke in the air. Resinous. Mineral. Austere.

Werwulf: The transformation. Skin, damp earth, root, resin, and the suggestion of wet fur. Intimate. Warm. Primal.

Blodwode: The memory of what the forest has witnessed. Bleeding tree bark, leather, musk, and the heat of flesh that was once human. Animalic. Resinous. Untamed.

The set is limited edition, $55, and won't ship until at least November 6, but at least that's in time for Grandma's Christmas present. You can also grab each perfume individually for $125.

It's not the first movie collaboration Heretic has done. Nosferatu Eau de Macabre used notes of "wilting lilacs, velvety vegan ambergris and strikes of lightning" while one for the The Bride promised "Jasmine and rose stitched together as flesh. Cedarwood as bone. Frankincense as breath or spirit." The company is perhaps most notorious for creating the viral “This Smells Like My Vagina” candle with Gwyneth Paltrow in 2020.

Rachel Weber is the Head of Editorial Development at IGN and an elder millennial. She's been a professional nerd since 2006 when she got her start on Official PlayStation Magazine in the UK, and has since worked for GamesIndustry.Biz, Rolling Stone and GamesRadar. She loves horror, horror movies, horror games, Red Dead Redemption 2, and her Love and Deepspace boyfriends.

articles.title: Tech layoffs 2026: Tracking the job losses across Microsoft, Netflix, Electronic Arts, eBay, Apple, Meta and others
articles.summary: There are only a couple of months left of the year and there have been over 195,000 layoffs across the tech industry. Here are the details.
articles.body:
We've only got a couple months left in 2026, but unfortunately we didn't get here without a ton of tech layoffs. In June, 14,000 job cuts happened at EV automaker Lucid, game developer Bungie, trading platform company Robinhood and others. Microsoft 's round of layoffs in July affected 4,800 jobs — mostly across its Xbox gaming division. Shortly after, companies including Samsung, Amazon, Uber and Monday.com followed suit.

According to many reports , the U.S. is at the center of these job cuts. Oracle has had the biggest impact on layoffs this year so far. The annual financial disclosure the company filed on June 23 showed the software giant cut 21,000 jobs over the past year, roughly 13% of its workforce.

"The adoption and deployment of AI technologies across our operations have resulted, and may continue to result, in reductions to our workforce," Oracle said in the filing.

In response to the numerous job cuts, California Governor Gavin Newsom in June unveiled a tool to track AI's impact on the workforce . "As AI advances, we aren't just watching from the sidelines; we're reimagining how we prepare California through strong governance and innovative policy." In addition, more than 4,500 Google workers signed a petition calling for layoff protections as things get worse. Some of the protections they're asking for include buyouts before mandatory layoffs and guaranteed severance.

TrueUp finds that layoffs seem to be moving at a faster rate than last year — over 245,000 workers in tech were let go in 2025, while there have been more than 195,000 layoffs in 2026 so far. Several of the companies below have laid off employees due to increased spending in AI. We'll get into the reasons for the layoffs.

While not officially new layoffs just yet, reports claim Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to 60,000 employees. This is in an effort to further reduce costs in the wake of increased AI usage. According to the reports, Xbox, Windows, Copilot and finance divisions will be participating in the offer. Microsoft already laid off thousands of workers so far in 2026.

EBay will reportedly cut 9% of its workforce in an effort to streamline operations. The latest job cuts come after a previous round of layoffs back in February, which affected about 800 positions. "As we work to capture the significant opportunity ahead, this step was taken to ensure we continue to operate from a position of strength by aligning our teams and resources with our top strategic priorities," an eBay spokesperson said in a statement.

Vide game publisher EA will eliminate 400 jobs , or about 3% of its workforce. This includes shutting down BioWare , the development studio behind the Mass Effect games. The next Mass Effect title will be cancelled as a result of the layoffs. These job cuts come after EA told investors earlier this year that it would reduce research and development costs as part of a plan to save upwards of $700 million.

According to a report in The Wall Street Journal, Netflix will lay off about 1,000 people, which accounts for about 6% of its global workforce. The report says the bulk of the layoffs will affect Netflix's "product, tech, legal and human-resources teams." This latest round of layoffs is the biggest for the company sinsce 2022, and it comes in the wake of Netflix struggling to increase customer engagement and overall growth.

A "large part" of the Airtable team was laid off on October 12. Federico Simionato, Airtable owner Bending Spoons' product leader, said on X that the layoffs were not due to the workers' abilities but rather the company's "deep belief that small teams ship more and better." The exact number of employees affected by the layoffs wasn't disclosed.

Amazon has reportedly laid off "fewer than 1,000 white-collar workers" in its stores division. That's the part of the company that oversees the tech giant's e-commerce website. Employees in the U.S., India and the United Kingdom were reportedly affected.

Workday will be laying off around 140 employees from the Bay Area, as part of an effort to trim its tech team. The cuts come as part of a broader plan to cut the company's global workforce by 2.5%.

Xbox announced it eliminated 268 roles across Halo Studios, other first-party studios and additional areas of the Xbox Game Studios division. These layoffs are part of a "reset" it announced this summer; the company already laid off 1,600 people in July, and said at the time that an additional 1,600 terminations were still to come.

According to a Bloomberg report , Apple has laid off an undisclosed number of employees from Fitness+, the company's exercise subscription service. According to the report, the layoffs affected those who worked in the audio side of the division, which includes features like Time to Walk and Time to Run guided audio workouts. Reportedly, offerings like this will be reduced — but not eliminated completely — from the service.

Oracle employees were impacted by yet another round of layoffs in September. The total number of employees laid off this time around is not currently known. The tech giant reportedly set employees early morning emails on Monday, September 14, letting those affected know it would be their last working day. It's also reported that, with these layoffs, Oracle is looking to offset the amount of money is pouring into AI chips and data centers. Earlier this year, Oracle laid off 21,000 people.

Uber announced it will cut 3,300 jobs, or about 10% of its workforce, in a big restructuring effort. "We are removing layers, simplifying team structures, refining our global location strategy, and focusing our people and investments against the biggest opportunities ahead of us," CEO Dara Khosrowshahi said in a statement . While the cuts apply to both regular employees and managers, the company stated it will reduce the "number of employees who sit 7+ layers from the CEO" by 20%, and it will cut the number of "micro-teams" by almost 50%. The CEO's memo did not mention AI as catalyst for the layoffs, but it did explain that this restructuring will allow Uber to bring its services to more people, invest in more drivers and merchants and "build the autonomous future."

According to an AppleInsider report , Apple laid off at least 60 people in its Vision Group, which is the team responsible for the Vision Pro VR headset. A Bloomberg report notes that Apple is also laying off roles in its Intelligent Systems Experience group, which is partially responsible for some of the AI systems on Apple devices. Overall, its estimated the layoffs affect more than 200 people.

When it comes to Vision Group and Vision Pro, it's been reported that incoming CEO John Ternus would be putting that product category "on ice," so this seems like the start of that process. The Vision Pro headset came out in 2024 with an eye-watering $3,699 starting price, and it remains to be seen if Apple will be pulling out of the AR/VR category entirely in the future. The Intelligence Systems changes are reportedly tied to changes that are necessary for the technical architecture for Apple's newly AI-infused Siri.

The New York Times reported that TikTok will lay off 250 people and close its Nashville, Tennessee office in October. This location was home to, in part, some of TikTok's content moderation team, although the company has not specified the reason for the layoffs or which teams they primarily affect. "We have decided to close our Nashville office to streamline our operations and better align our teams for long-term growth," a press officer for what is known as the TikTok U.S.D.S. Joint Venture said in a statement to the Times.

Zillow will lay off just over 500 people as it enacts organizational changes across the company. "These are difficult decisions that reflect both the strides we're making in our strategy and the reality of what is required of us to grow at scale," CEO Jeremy Wacksman wrote in a press release . Wacksman didn't go into detail about what organizational changes were made, or which departments are bearing the brunt of the layoffs. "These changes are about ensuring we have a disciplined cost structure and getting more efficient, with the right people in the right positions," he wrote.

Etsy laid off about 220 people, or 12% of its workforce, as it attempts to simplify its organizational structure. The cuts primarily affected the product and engineering teams, and Etsy CEO Kruti Patel Goyal said that the layoffs were necessary to build "the organization we believe Etsy needs for the future." An Etsy spokesperson told CNBC that the cuts were not driven by artificial intelligence adoption.

Microsoft has begun another round of layoffs that affects 4,800 jobs , or around 2.1% of its workforce. The Xbox division is getting hit the hardest, with 3,200 roles getting cut through fiscal year 2027, Xbox chief Asha Sharma said in a post on X — 1,600 people were let go on July 6. Shortly after those layoffs were revealed, it was announced that Sharma was appointed to a U.S. Federal Reserve task force to help advise it on "productivity and jobs." Other appointees include Marc Andreessen of Andreessen Horowitz and Charles I. Jones, professor of economics at Stanford University.

Intel is reportedly downsizing its data center group, despite strong performance. The company hasn't disclosed how many roles would be affected.

Visa will be cutting about 2,600 jobs, which amounts to about 7% of its workforce. The layoffs will primarily affect the technology and product teams, and the impetus in part is to make the company more efficient. "To capture the opportunities ahead and best position Visa to lead this transformation, we must continue evolving how we work," Chief Executive Officer Ryan McInerney wrote in a memo. "AI is also helping to accelerate this evolution and shape the way work gets done at Visa." But according to Bloomberg's report, AI was not the only factor to influence Visa's decision to do these layoffs. The company reportedly intends to reinvest in things like consumer payments and value-added services like stablecoin.

Software company Monday.com will be laying off 20% of its workforce, which comes out to about 630 people. This comes as the company makes a pivot to AI and is attempting to make its AI platform a core offering of its business. Earlier this year, it designed its main product around the idea that business customers increasingly want its employees to work with AI agents.

Patreon laid off 20% of its workforce, or 93 people, as a result of the company "changing our organizational structure and how we work." But Patreon was explicit in its email to creators and staff that "we are not making the above changes because we believe AI replaces humans." However, the email also said "AI has fundamentally transformed the tech industry, though, including how we work."

Uber has reportedly laid off 10% of its customer service division, according to a Bloomberg report, as it looks to "embrace artificial intelligence" and simplify its ranks. The company also stated in May that it would slow hiring as it makes use of AI more internally.

Samsung is eliminating 179 jobs as it moves its New Jersey headquarters to Texas later this year. The move is expected to impact around 1,000 workers. We're now getting a fuller picture of what that looks like: according to Reuters , 739 roles at Samsung's New Jersey location have been affected in some way. Some have been offered relocation packages as the company shifts its headquarters to Texas, while others have been let go. In addition, it's reported that 100 roles in its Texas location, primarily in the mobile division, have also been let go.

Amazon will lay off some people in its artificial general intelligence group, although the company has not disclosed how many roles will be affected. "This is a fast-moving space, and we're sharpening our focus on the initiatives that matter most for customers, so we can move faster on what counts," an Amazon spokesperson told CNBC.

Sony Interactive Entertainment released a statement that it's cutting "a significant number of employees" from its Bungie workforce. That includes most of the Destiny team and some Marathon team members, as well as SIE teams that support Bungie's operations. The email didn't say how many employees were affected.

Electric vehicle maker Lucid announced it's cutting around 18% of its workforce, and also noted COO Marc Winterhoff's leaving the company, Reuters reported . The layoffs are in an effort to "​boost profitability amid growing competition." The cuts affect full-time employees, contractors and hourly manufacturing workers.

Cloud computing services company Rackspace laid off 750 workers , or around 15% of its workforce. The cuts are driven by a shift in focus toward AI.

EV company Rivian let go of hundreds of employees , which amounts to around 2% of the company's workforce, the Wall Street Journal reported . Those affected were part of Rivian's service and customer organization, which handled marketing and sales.

Trading platform company Robinhood is planning to lay off 10% of its staff to restructure, the Robinhood Comms account shared on X today — that's around 290 jobs. It's unclear if the layoffs are AI-related, but CEO Vlad Tenev noted the company will be "utilizing frontier technologies to push our execution even further."

Salesforce laid off at least 86 employees in California, though Business Insider sources say job cuts also occurred in Washington and outside the U.S. as well. The cuts reportedly affect employees involved with Salesforce's Agentforce AI product, Mulesoft IT integration tool and its Marketing Cloud software.

Groupon is planning to lay off roughly 25% of its workforce , which will result in 400 job cuts. Those positions are expected to be eliminated by the end of the third quarter. This is in an effort to restructure the company and rebuild it as an AI-native company.

In another set of AI-related layoffs, website builder Wix said it was cutting around 20% of staff. Wix cofounder and CEO Avishai Abrahami announced the cuts on X , pointing to the changes AI is bringing to the industry and stating "we need to become a faster, leaner, and flatter organization." He also put part of the blame on the Israeli Shekel to U.S. Dollar exchange rates, which impact the company because it's based in Israel. The cuts are expected to impact around 1,000 roles, based on Wix's headcount.

Webflow, a website builder and hosting company, conducted a round of layoffs that an employee called "a bloodbath" in a statement to the San Francisco Chronicle . It's unclear how many employees were impacted, but one anonymous developer from the company told the Chronicle they believe it was larger than Webflow's last major round of layoffs, which affected 8% of its workforce in 2024. As with other recent layoffs, it looks like a shift to AI is to blame here. "AI is rewriting the rules for how marketing teams create, test, and optimize digital experiences," CEO Linda Tong said in a statement . "And the companies that move decisively through moments like this are the ones that come out ahead."

ClickUp CEO Zeb Evans announced that the company cut 22% of its workforce as it turns toward AI to improve productivity. He claimed it "wasn't about cutting costs," but about funneling savings from the cuts "directly back into the people who stay." The company has introduced million-dollar salary bands reserved for employees who "create outsized impact using AI."

Intuit is planning to lay off 3,000 employees, or about 17% of its workforce, Reuters reports . CEO Sasan Goodarzi sent a memo to employees noting the layoffs would help the company's efforts of focusing on infusing AI across its services.

Meta has officially begun cutting 10% of its workforce , totaling around 8,000 employees. In addition, it plans to close 6,000 open roles. The reason is to allow more room for AI spending.

Like Microsoft, NPR is offering voluntary buyouts to 300 employees in the newsroom, but only 30 will be accepted. However, if the news organization doesn't receive its target number, it will result in targeted layoffs. The reason is due to the loss of federal funding.

The online retail giant cut more jobs this month, this time from the Selling Partner Services organization. These new layoffs come after Amazon cut roughly 30,000 jobs in rounds across October and January. A spokesperson told Business Insider that the most recent layoffs have affected a "small number" of employees. The Selling Partner Services team works with third-party merchants on Amazon, providing onboarding, logistics and account management support.

Cisco is cutting just under 4,000 jobs in Q4, CEO Chuck Robbins said in a blog post . Impacted employees will receive pro-rated payment of 2026 bonuses and will also receive "support in finding new opportunities" via Cisco's placement services. In June, it was confirmed that the layoffs include 471 workers in the Bay Area .

"While we are reducing roles in some areas, we are making clear, strategic investments — particularly in silicon, optics, security, and in our employees' use of AI across the company," Robbins said.

LinkedIn is planning to lay off 5% of its staff, which is around 875 employees, Reuters reports . An anonymous person told Reuters the reason is to reorganize teams and focus employees on areas ⁠where its business is growing. However, one of the sources said the reason was "not for artificial intelligence to replace jobs at LinkedIn."

GM is letting go of around 500 to 600 employees in the Information Technology sector, Bloomberg reports . The reason is to "trim costs and clear the way to bring in staff with skills in other technology areas."

Due to restructuring driven by AI, Cloudflare is cutting more than 1,100 employees . "Today's actions are not a cost-cutting exercise or an assessment of individuals' performance; They are about Cloudflare defining how a world-class, high-growth company operates and creates value in the agentic AI era," Prince and President Michelle Zatlyn said in an email to employees .

PayPal is planning to cut around 20% of its staff — nearly 4,800 employees — over the next few years, according to the Wall Street Journal . "First, we will remove duplication and layers from our organizational structure. Second, we will accelerate our AI adoption and automation across our operations," CEO Enrique Lores said to investors.

Cryptocurrency platform Coinbase is laying off 700 employees , which amounts to around 14% of its staff. CEO Brian Armstrong cites the current market and AI changing the way they work as reasons for the layoffs.

Microsoft is offering a first-ever buyout to up to 7% of its employees, CNBC reports . It's a one-time retirement program that's available for workers at the senior director level and below whose years of employment and age are 70 or higher.

Nike announced it's laying off 1,400 people this week. "Collectively, these changes will result in a reduction of approximately 1,400 roles in global operations, with the majority in technology," COO Venkatesh Alagirisamy said. "These reductions are very hard for the teammates directly affected and for the teams around them, too."

Amazon is planning to temporarily close a warehouse in Homestead, Florida, which will eliminate more than 600 jobs, Newsweek reports . The job cuts will start in July and continue through September but the giant company is giving employees the option to relocate to other facilities. The warehouse has only been open for just under two years but Amazon is already looking to update the site.

Battery recycling company Redwood Materials laid off 10% of its employees, totaling 135 people, TechCrunch reports . Those who were let go received an email from the chief HR officer telling them the layoffs were made "to sharpen our focus, our work and the size of our teams to support the direction Redwood is going in the future."

Snap is laying off 1,000 workers , which is 16% of its staff, Variety reports . The Snapchat parent company made the announcement just weeks after Irenic Capital Management asked the company to make changes to improve performance and revenue.

Snap is using AI to streamline operations and assist the now smaller workforce. "We have already witnessed small squads leveraging AI tools to drive meaningful progress across several important initiatives," Snap CEO Evan Spiegel said.

Just two months after taking over as CEO of Disney, Josh D'Amaro announced the company is laying off 1,000 of its employees, AP News reports . In addition, Marvel let 8% of its staff go after the call was made.

"Over the past several months, we have looked at ways in which we can streamline our operations in various parts of the company to ensure we deliver the world-class creativity and innovation our fans value and expect from Disney," D'Amaro said in a memo to employees. "Given the fast-moving pace of our industries, this requires us to constantly assess how to foster a more agile and technologically-enabled workforce to meet tomorrow's needs."

The wearable camera maker this year will eliminate 145 employees due to a restructuring plan to cut costs, the Wall Street Journal reported . The cuts are expected to last until the end of the year.

Vimeo is going through its third round of layoffs since it was acquired by Bending Spoons. This time, the company let go of more than 120 people, which is about 25% of its city staff .

It's been reported that 200 Meta employees in the Bay Area will lose their jobs at the end of May. That includes 124 employees in Burlingame and 74 in Sunnyvale. The company last laid off workers just a few weeks ago.

Oracle has begun implementing a big cull of its employee base . On the final day of March, more than a dozen Oracle employees announced on LinkedIn they had been let go from their jobs, Business Insider reports . It's unclear at this time how many workers were affected, but it was projected to be thousands at the start of this month.

Those laid off received the same email : "After careful consideration of Oracle's current business needs, we have made the decision to eliminate your role as part of a broader organizational change."

The job cuts are reportedly to help Oracle stem a cash drain related its expenditures on AI infrastructure. In June, Oracle revealed that it had laid off 21,000 people as part of the cuts.

Deux Ex studio Eidos-Montréal announced on March 30 that it's laying off 124 people . In response, the studio head David Anfossi has decided to leave the company.

The cuts are a result of "changing project needs and impacts across production and support teams," the gaming company said in a LinkedIn post . It also noted that the decision to lay off these employees is not related to their talent or performance.

After already having layoffs in January , T-Mobile has cut even more of its workers, GeekWire reports . It's unclear how many people were laid off at this time, but it could be in the hundreds.

"To move even faster in a dynamic market while continuing to deliver best-in-class digital experiences for our customers, we're further aligning our IT organization to support future growth and innovation… This includes the difficult decision of eliminating some roles while continuing to invest and hire in areas," T-Mobile told GeekWire in a statement.

Meta began laying off hundreds of employees on March 25, totaling around 700 people, per The New York Times . Those impacted were part of the Reality Labs team, as well as social media and recruiting teams. Though still significant, this is a much smaller number compared to a Reuters report that suggested 20% off staff would be affected by layoffs due to the increased spending on AI.

This change comes as the company is shifting away from its metaverse creation, which includes Horizon Worlds for its Quest VR headset that's operated by the Reality Labs team.

The gaming giant on March 24 announced it was laying off more than 1,000 workers in an effort to right-size the staff of its popular free-to-play online shooter, Fortnite. CEO Tim Sweeney sent a note to his staff, citing the reason for the layoffs is due to the "downturn in Fortnite engagement," which means "we're spending significantly more than we're making, and we have to make major cuts to keep the company funded." He made it a point to note the layoffs are not related to AI.

105 employees from the Red Storm Entertainment team were laid off by Ubisoft in an effort to cut costs, IGN reports . Game development has ended at the studio, so the downsizing will remain permanent. The company employed 180 people in 2022 but has seen multiple layoffs over the years.

Roughly 1,600 employees were laid off at Atlassian on March 16, which is around 10% of total workers. Ahead of the layoffs, Atlassian CEO Mike Cannon-Brookes shared a message with the entire team, letting them know the reason is to "self-fund further investment in AI and enterprise sales, while strengthening our financial profile. We're also changing the way we work and reorganising around our System of Work to move faster." Impacted employees received an email shortly after this message went out.

images.caption: Tech layoffs are hitting hard this year as the industry shifts to accommodate the rapidly increasing capabilities of AI. (NurPhoto via Getty Images)

articles.title: Dragonproof Is a Perfect Fusion of Gargoyles and Buffy the Vampire Slayer
articles.summary: Check out an exclusive preview of Dragonproof, a new fantasy graphic novel perfect for fans of Gargoyles, Buffy, and Fourth Wing.
articles.body:
AHOY Comics has a promising new fantasy graphic novel in the works, and it's billed as a fusion of '90s classics like Gargoyles and Buffy the Vampire Slayer. That book is Dragonproof, and IGN has an exclusive preview.

Check out the slideshow gallery below for an early look at Dragonproof:

Dragonproof Graphic Novel Preview Gallery

Dragonproof is a collaboration between writer Eric Palicki (Black's Myth) and artist Giulia Lalli (Eight Limbs). This 96-page graphic novel features TPB cover art by Tango and HC cover art by Lalli. Here's the official description of the book:

Somewhere in the Pacific Northwest on an ill-fate camping trip, Ashleigh Cole stumbles upon a dying dragon in the woods, its hide peppered with bullet wounds and tattooed with U.S. military markings. Ash returns to her mundane life, convinced her experience in the woods was all just a hallucination—until she begins to display some oddly dragonlike characteristics herself. Compelled by voices in her mind, Ash undertakes a mission to rescue other captive dragons and help the mythical creatures escape—but the shadowy government organization determined to turn them into weapons of mass destruction has other plans. Funny, heartfelt, and action-packed, DRAGONPROOF will appeal to adult readers who grew up on Buffy and Gargoyles and capture the imagination of post-YA readers of The Fourth Wing, ACOTAR, and more.

“Like so much of my other work, DRAGONPROOF is, at its heart, about outsiders finding their people and their purpose,” said Palicki in a statement. “I tend to wear my influences on my sleeve, and this book is also a love letter to some of the stories that made me the writer I am today. Having partners in Giulia and Gab who were on the same wavelength was pure magic.”

Jesse is a mild-mannered staff writer for IGN. Allow him to lend a machete to your intellectual thicket by following @jschedeen on BlueSky .

articles.title: Matthew Lillard Calls His Superman 2 Character 'A Very James Gunn Moment'
articles.summary: Superman 2: Man of Tomorrow brings Daredevil: Born Again actor Matthew Lillard into the wider James Gunn DCU, but comic fans might not recognize his character.
articles.body:
Superman 2: Man of Tomorrow brings Daredevil: Born Again actor Matthew Lillard into the wider James Gunn DCU, but comic fans might not recognize his character. Man of Tomorrow mixes a returning cast with fresh characters as David Corenswelt’s Superman agrees to an unsteady alliance with Nicholas Hoult's Lex Luthor.

Brainiac is the antagonist this time, giving us a bigger-brained baddie than Superman’s bald-headed human rival. A guy with a bigger brain is basically Luthor’s own kryptonite.

Rachel Brosnahan will return as Lois Lane and Skyler Gisondo is back as Jimmy Olsen. These returning cast members will bump into players from the wider DCU, including Blue Beetle and the Justice Gang. Matthew Lillard’s role in all this, however, has not been announced.

On a promotional tour for Prime Video’s adaptation of Carrie, Lillard was asked whether his character is someone comic fans will recognise or not. Fan theories that he would play the DCU’s Barry Allen were previously shot down by DC Studios co-CEO James Gunn.

"It's a very James Gunn moment,” Lillard told The Direct . “So, I wouldn't worry too much about finding him in the comics."

While short and sweet, it does suggest Lillard will play an original character, rather than someone already established in the comics. Gunn has already introduced a range of original characters to the DCU, including Amanda Waller's daughter and Mister Handsome.

Gunn recently shot down rumors that Milly Alcock had been fired from her role as Supergirl . "Oh brother," his post said at the time. "You guys just have to stop listening to BS, and I'm mostly done shooting down rumors, as there are so many and I'm not on here much."

Man of Tomorrow is scheduled to be released in theaters on July 9, 2027.

Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

articles.title: 'A Lot of Players Don't Want to Play a Monster' – WoW Forever Principal Designer Sheds More Light on Why the Skyborne Were Added
articles.summary: World of Warcraft Forever has its full launch a week from now on November 4, but ahead of time, Blizzard principal game designer Kris Zierhut shared a little bit of insight on why the new Skyborne race was added to the game.
articles.body:
World of Warcraft Forever has its full launch a week from now on November 4, but ahead of time, Blizzard principal game designer Kris Zierhut shared a little bit of insight on why the new Skyborne race was added to the game.

When I asked Zierhut about Skyborne's addition, he told me that the goal was to add more elves to the game but to maintain the faction balance in the process. "We knew that we wanted to bring in more of the elves into the game. We know they're the most popular races in World of Warcraft historically. And in particular, the current alliance and Horde races from the Classic Era have the unfortunate feature that they tend to cause a faction imbalance," he told me.

As for why Blizzard needed to add elves specifically, it's because there's a segment of the player base that doesn't want to play some of WoW's more unique races. Zierhut explained, "There's a certain... a lot of players who don't want to play a monster, to put it really honestly. They don't want to be an Orc or a Troll or a Tauren or Undead. They want to have something that looks prettier. It's not everybody."

There are other possibilities for elves in Azeroth, like the Blood Elves, but the Forever team doesn't want to step on the retail team's toes. Elsewhere in the interview, I asked about Silvermoon, the home of the Blood Elves, and Zierhut referenced that, saying, "You mentioned Silvermoon, and this is a story that Retail had recently told, and we didn't want to get in each other's way of telling that story. We want to give them time to let their Silvermoon story breathe and do everything they wanted with it. And then once they were done with it, we could maybe then go visit Silvermoon."

So, it sounds like there's a chance that the Blood Elves could come to the game in the future, but for now, players will just have to make do with the Skyborne if they want a Horde elf race.

Ahead of Forever coming out next week, Blizzard has also detailed how often players can expect new updates , which will be added slower than the quick eight-week patch cycle of the modern game. Zierhut has also told me that the Forever team is looking at visiting some of the locations we've been to in expansions, like Northrend and Pandaria , in future updates.

Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

articles.title: Best Buy’s Black Friday Sale Schedule Announced
articles.summary: Best Buy has taken to its corporate blog to announce the retailer's full holiday sale schedule, including Black Friday and last-minute Christmas sales.
articles.body:
Retailers have begun to announce their Black Friday sale schedules. Following hot on the heels of Walmart's announcement this morning, Best Buy has unveiled its entire holiday 2026 sale schedule — including Black Friday. It’s comprised of several sale events that run between October 30 and December 24.

Here’s the full Best Buy holiday sale schedule:

November 6 - November 19 : Early Black Friday Deals + Doorbusters

November 19 - 28 : Black Friday Doorbusters + Deals

November 29 - 30 : Cyber Monday Sale Event

December 18 - 24 : Last-Minute Savings Event

The sales kick off with the DoorBOOsters sale that runs October 30 through November 1. We don’t have details about what deals will be available at this point, but we'll be sure to cover the sales right here at IGN.

Following a brief five-day break, the official “Early Black Friday Deals + Doorbusters” sale begins on November 6. This sounds like a general sale that will run all month. However, Best Buy says “new deals will drop every Friday” during this time.

The actual Black Friday Doorbusters and Deals sale starts on November 19 and runs through November 28 (the day after Black Friday). These will be the real deals, though based on previous years, you can generally expect new deals to go live on Black Friday itself (November 27).

If stock holds out, Black Friday deals typically stay live throughout the weekend. Best Buy’s Cyber Monday Sale Event kicks off Sunday, November 29 and runs through Monday, November 30. These deals are not typically very different from the Black Friday deals, though some retailers get resupplies of stock on Cyber Monday. So if you missed out on any Black Friday deals, it’s worth checking back on Monday to see if it’s available again.

It’s also worth noting that, if you happen to be a Best Buy Plus or Total member , you’ll earn double rewards on purchases from November 19 to December 6.

After effectively an entire month of sales at Best Buy, the retailer is giving it a rest through the first two weeks of December. But starting December 18 and running through December 24 (aka Christmas Eve), you can expect to see more deals go live in what Best Buy is calling its Last-Minute Savings sale.

If you buy something from Best Buy between October 30 - December 31 and want to return it, you have until January 15 to make the return for most items. You can find more details about what to expect from the sale in Best Buy’s corporate blog post .

articles.title: The Dune: Part Three Final Trailer Reveals Just How Different This Sequel Is
articles.summary: The final trailer for Dune: Part Three reveals just how different this sequel will be from the books, and it all centers around Zendaya's Chani and her children.
articles.body:
Denis Villeneuve’s Dune: Part Three may ostensibly be an adaptation of author Frank Herbert’s novel Dune Messiah, but it’s been clear from the start that this sequel is going to make some major deviations from its source material. That fact is made even more abundantly clear with the release of the final trailer for Dune: Part Three, which teases the role Chani (Zendaya) and her children will play in this massive intergalactic conflict.

How different will this sequel be from the source material, and what role will these Fremen radicals play? Here’s what the new trailer tells us.

Again, it was obvious from the moment the credits rolled on 2024’s Dune: Part Two that the third and final act of Villeneuve’s trilogy would be blazing new ground for the franchise. That’s because the second film leaves Zendaya’s character in a very different place compared to the books.

Part Two wraps with a disillusioned Chani leaving her lover Paul (Timothée Chalamet) and returning to the Arakeen desert. Unlike Stilgar (Javier Bardem) and his fellow fundamentalists, Chani is not a believer in Paul’s jihad, and she’s heartbroken that he went back on his word not to claim power for himself. But in the original Dune novel, Chani remains by Paul’s side, relishing her role as his faithful concubine even as Paul marries Princess Irulan (Florence Pugh) to cement his claim to the throne.

That film set up Chani to play a vastly different role in Dune: Part Three. Rather than being Paul’s lover and confidant, she’s estranged from him. Rather than struggling to conceive a child as Irulan poisons her with contraceptives, Chani is safe from Irulan’s grasp and is raising two children, Leto II (Nakota-Wolf Momoa) and Ghanima (Ida Brooke).

The fact that Paul and Chani have two teenage children during this adaptation of Dune Messiah is arguably an even bigger change to the source material. In the books, Leto II and Ghanima don’t fully come into play until the third novel, Children of Dune. And they fill a very different role there. In Children of Dune, the characters are somewhat younger, and they’re held up by the Fremen as Paul’s rightful successors. It’s a burden neither is quite ready to accept at first, at least until Leto II becomes radicalized during the course of the story and resurfaces as a superhuman crusader ready to finish what his father started.

None of that seems to apply in Dune: Part Three. Here, both children are older and clearly standing in direct opposition to their father. We can only guess as to how characters like Stilgar will react upon learning of their existence. Either way, both have their part to play as Paul struggles to steer his religious crusade and his enemies plot against him.

So how exactly do Chani and her children factor into the plot? The final trailer is actually pretty revealing on that front. Previous trailers focused mainly on the initial fight between Chani and Paul post-Dune: Part Two, along with glimpses of the two battling one another in the deserts of Arrakis. But the final trailer confirms one very important detail. It tells us that Chani is actively participating in the plot against Paul.

As in Dune Messiah, Dune: Part Three focuses on an alliance of Paul’s enemies, including Irulan, Reverend Mother Gaius Helen Mohaim (Charlotte Rampling), and a Tleilaxu face dancer (or shapeshifter) named Scytale (Robert Pattinson). Their goal is to destabilize Paul’s regime and force him to abdicate the throne by any means necessary. Part of that plot involves the resurrection of Duncan Idaho (Jason Momoa), who now takes the form of a ghola (essentially a clone with mental conditioning) named Hayt.

The fact that Chani and her children are involved in this plot is a huge change for the Dune franchise. But what is their end goal here? We don’t get the impression that Chani is necessarily trying to kill Paul. She still holds a great love for him, despite Paul being responsible for billions of deaths and untold carnage. She and the twins seem to have a different goal in mind.

The trailer makes it appear that Chani and her Fremen loyalists have been tapped to help steal a sandworm from the desert. We see a massive machine shooting mechanical ropes into the sand, so the goal is probably to lure a sandworm, ensnare it, and take it offworld.

This plot makes sense. Paul may have a massive army of well-trained fanatics, but the real source of his power is that he maintains a stranglehold on the galaxy’s supply of spice. As they say, “He who controls the spice controls the universe.” Scytale clearly hopes to break Paul’s monopoly on spice and give his alliance some added leverage against the emperor.

Whether or not Chani and her children are ultimately successful in their sandworm heist (likely they won’t be), we suspect that their team-up with Scytale and his allies will collapse by the end of the film. Scytale has no compunction about killing Paul, whereas Chani probably only wants him to step down and reunite their family. The real question is whether her ultimate fate will be similar to that of the book. At this point, Dune fans can take nothing for granted with this sequel.

For more, learn why the Game of Thrones movie needs to take inspiration from Dune in order to succeed .

Jesse is a mild-mannered staff writer for IGN. Allow him to lend a machete to your intellectual thicket by following @jschedeen on BlueSky .

articles.title: 'Physical Books, But Not Physical Games?' — PlayStation Book Announcement Prompts Confusion Over Sony's Physical Media Stance
articles.summary: Preorders have opened for PlayStation: The First 30 Years, a physical book honoring the gaming giant’s tenured history, but fans aren't exactly in a celebratory mood.
articles.body:
Preorders have opened for PlayStation: The First 30 Years, a physical book honoring the gaming giant’s tenured history, but fans aren't exactly in a celebratory mood. The book’s announcement comes as Sony faces continued criticism for its decision to cut disc production , prompting confusion over the new physical media release and an influx of “No Disc, No Buy” replies.

The book itself is a collaboration between PlayStation and Read-Only Memory, a UK-based publisher focused on “premium” gaming and world-building books. A widely available Standard edition is listed at $125, while a Deluxe Edition, listed at $325, will only be available in 1994 copies. Both editions are now up for preorder exclusively from Read-Only Memory , shipping this November.

According to the official listing , the 400-page book “is the definitive visual chronicle of Sony’s world-changing videogame console, marking its 30th anniversary with unprecedented access to the company’s archive of R&D prototypes, concept sketches, and development models.” It collects “insights from the engineers and designers who shaped PlayStation’s identity,” including the “Father of PlayStation,” Ken Kutaragi, the original DualShock designer, Teiyu Goto, and the chief designer on the PS5, Yujin Morisawa.

Sneak peek images show early designs of DualShock controllers and PlayStation consoles — complete with beautiful disc drives.

Fans were quick to point out the curious decision to celebrate the gaming brand’s history with a physical media release. “Just selling collectibles and taking away what we actually want to collect,” said one X user with a sequence of disc emojis. “Just so we’re clear… You support physical books, but not physical games?” replied another.

Earlier this year, Sony announced that it would be cutting disc production for PlayStation consoles starting in 2028. Despite immediate backlash, Sony has stood by the decision. But gamers refuse to back down, taking over the comment sections on pretty much anything PlayStation-related .

While the online backlash is louid, it remains to be seen whether it will affect future launches of physical collectibles, digital games, or even the PS6. Ken Kutaragi, who is featured in the new book, recently backed the studio’s decision , acknowledging that “physical discs have become a metaphor for ‘owning’ games” but ultimately seeing the decision to cut production as “economically reasonable.”

While PlayStation has seen a continued decline in physical disc sales , critics argue that “ownership” is an essential part of gaming communities . Building up your physical game collection has long been a source of pride for any PlayStation, Xbox, or Nintendo fan, while also allowing for sharing and re-selling.

Former PlayStation boss Shawn Layden has been one voice speaking out against the business decision, saying, “If you can't sell a thing, it means you don't own a thing. If you don't own it, then what are you buying?” As PlayStation continues to look back on its 30-year-history, it’s clear that this decision will define its future.

Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

articles.title: Discord Messages in Discoverable Servers Will Soon Be Searchable on Google
articles.summary: Over the last decade, Discord has become the de facto community space for gaming, and there are a lot of huge servers out there that you can find by scrolling through its public servers page. But starting on November 16, some messages in these huge servers will be viewable from Google.
articles.body:
Over the last decade, Discord has become the de facto community space for gaming, and there are a lot of huge servers out there that you can find by scrolling through its public servers page . But starting on November 16, some messages in these huge servers will be viewable from Google.

In a blog post , Discord laid out its plans to publish 'Server Web Pages' for every discoverable server on Discord by default. These are bespoke web pages that give a preview of a server's contents before forcing users to hit the join button. There are already several of these pages live, typically for huge online games like Rust or Dead by Daylight . These pages will be discoverable on Google, and will display a summary of the discussions going on in the server.

But while these 'Server Web Pages' will be going live next month, another update is coming in December, that'll allow answers to questions to appear in Google search. According to the blog post, "answers to questions your members sent in public channels can be found in a web search, in their own words. Server admins decide which channels take part, and server members can choose whether their own messages appear. Usernames and avatars will not be shown alongside these messages."

It's important to note that only large discoverable servers will be affected by these changes, meaning your World of Warcraft guild or friend group probably won't be affected in any way. Discoverable server admins can opt out their servers or even individual channels by going to Server Settings, then Web Presence and choosing which channels you want to be visible. But, if you don't change anything, public channels will have the setting enabled by default.

If you're just a user in one of these huge servers, and you don't want your messages to be viewable from Google, you can also opt your own messages out. Simply go to User Settings, then Data and Privacy and disable 'Show my message content from Discoverable channels on web pages.'

Discord is introducing this feature to help people find answers to questions. If you've Googled anything in the last couple of years, you've probably noticed that a lot of search results for questions will lead you to Reddit, or another similar message board. It seems like Discord wants a slice of that pie.

According to the blog, "prior to Discord's launch, message boards were common, ranging from community-driven forums to official ones run by game studios. These message boards excelled at hosting long-form, structured conversations about helping people, theory crafting, and more. While they still exist today, many have moved into Discord servers. This has led to valuable information being locked in Discord conversations, inaccessible to the wider internet. We want to fix this."

There will likely be some useful information that you'll be able to find when these changes go live in December, but there are definitely some privacy concerns, as well. So, if you don't want your messages in large discoverable servers to be seen by everyone, make sure to disable the feature today, before all the changes go live. So far, these changes will be exclusive to large public servers with more than 1,000 members, and hopefully it stays that way.

articles.title: Brewers seek first World Series sweep since Giants swept Tigers in 2012
articles.summary: There have been 19 sweeps in the World Series, plus two more in 1907 and 1922 that finished 4-0 with a tie game. The Brewers could get the 20th sweep tonight...
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers will have the chance to do something that hasn't been done in 14 years when they take the field for Game 4 of the World Series on Tuesday, Oct. 27.

With a 3-0 series lead over the Tampa Bay Rays after a 10-1 win in Game 3 , the Brewers could become the first team to sweep a World Series opponent since 2012, when the San Francisco Giants swept the Detroit Tigers . That year, the Brewers finished third in the National League Central and missed the playoffs.

There have been 19 sweeps in the World Series, plus two more in 1907 and 1922 that ended 4-0 with a tie game, according to Baseball Almanac. Of those 21 series, the New York Yankees were involved in 11 – eight as the winning team and three as the losing team.

If the Brewers complete the sweep of the Rays, it would end a 14-year World Series sweep drought, the longest in series history. The next-longest gap is 13 years, from 1976 to 1989.

No team has ever lost a World Series after taking a 3-0 lead and only four teams have won Game 4 after falling behind 3-0: the 1910 Chicago Cubs, 1937 New York Giants, 1970 Cincinnati Reds and 2024 New York Yankees. In each case, the team that had been leading, 3-0, went on to win Game 5.

Milwaukee Brewers vs. Tampa Bay Rays highlights, World Series Game 3

Here's a rundown of all the sweeps in World Series history:

2012: San Francisco Giants over Detroit Tigers

2007: Boston Red Sox over Colorado Rockies

2005: Chicago White Sox over Houston Astros

2004: Boston Red Sox over St. Louis Cardinals

1999: New York Yankees over Atlanta Braves

1998: New York Yankees over San Diego Padres

1990: Cincinnati Reds over Oakland Athletics

1989: Oakland Athletics over San Francisco Giants

1976: Cincinnati Reds over New York Yankees

1966: Baltimore Orioles over Los Angeles Dodgers

1963: Los Angeles Dodgers over New York Yankees

1954: New York Giants over Cleveland Indians

1950: New York Yankees over Philadelphia Phillies

1938: New York Yankees over Chicago Cubs

1932: New York Yankees over Chicago Cubs

1927: New York Yankees over Pittsburgh Pirates

1922: New York Giants over New York Yankees (with 1 tie)

articles.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Adds Series Favorite Map, Shipment, to Multiplayer
articles.summary: Shipment, one of Call of Duty's most iconic maps, has officially been added to Modern Warfare 4's multiplayer.
articles.body:
Shipment, one of Call of Duty's most iconic maps, has officially been added to Modern Warfare 4's multiplayer.

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's Shipment is now available in the standard 6v6 map rotation, as well as in a playlist known as Shipment 24/7. Call of Duty fans are likely well-versed in the latter, which allows players to exclusively play Shipment, with the only variable being the mode you play. The playlist is preferred for camo and challenge grinding, as you can just farm kills ad nauseam. Needless to say, it should be pure chaos, just the way Shipment fans like it.

You know what to do 😤 Shipment is LIVE NOW in #MW4 — Call of Duty (@CallofDuty) October 27, 2026

You know what to do 😤 Shipment is LIVE NOW in #MW4

The map was introduced back in 2007, nearly 20 years ago, and was reportedly a total accident. The map was meant to be a simple test environment for certain features like split-screen, but was mistakenly left in the final build. This was right before the days of constant game updates, and if a developer did want to make a change, it cost money. So... it stayed. Fans liked it, and then it became iconic for its fast-paced, chaotic nature. It has returned in a number of Call of Duty games, but is a prominent staple of the recently rebooted Modern Warfare saga.

Shipment makes for the first post-launch map in MW4, but more is on the way. The game's first season of post-launch content will debut next week. We don't currently know what will be part of the first season, but you can likely expect new weapons, a battle pass, skins, and potentially new maps and modes, if history is anything to go by.

IGN posted its full review of Modern Warfare 4's campaign and multiplayer the other day, giving the two modes a collective 7/10. Although the review praised the campaign, it noted that the multiplayer didn't push the franchise forward in any major ways, despite still being fun.

"The new shape-shifting Kill Block arena is certainly a highlight, but elsewhere very little has been offered when it comes to innovation or interesting map design. It’s still that familiar Call of Duty brand of fun, just not in any way I haven’t seen before. Overall, it’s a good package from Infinity Ward, with a great campaign as its highlight, ensuring Modern Warfare 4’s place as one of Call of Duty’s better recent entries."

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: Life Is Strange Developer Don't Nod Blasted by Union Employees Over 'Illegal' Management Practices as Possible Layoffs Loom
articles.summary: An October 27 statement from employees of Don't Nod, the developer best known for making the original Life is Strange games, warn that the company is in danger of insolvency and layoffs, and accused its management of "illegal" practices that have caused staff "uncertainty and anxiety."
articles.body:
An October 27 statement from employees of Don't Nod, the developer best known for making the original Life is Strange games, warn that the company is in danger of insolvency and layoffs, and accused its management of "illegal" practices that have caused staff "uncertainty and anxiety."

The damning statement comes from employees who are members of the French game industry union Le Syndicat des Travailleureuses du Jeu Vidéo, which revealed that Don’t Nod is currently under a safeguard to help protect itself from insolvency (meaning that the company wouldn’t be able to pay its debts).

The statement claims employees were approached by management and given “several financial scenarios” that could happen in the near future, both of which “included redundancies," with the worst case forecasting the “liquidation of the company through 2026.”

The message states that “nearly all of the non-managerial jobs” were cut at Don’t Nod, which reportedly included all animators, character artists, concept artists, associate producers, and most environmental artists, sound designers, level designers, programmers, QA testers, HR and developers. Half of its game designers were also laid off, according to the statement.

“Management is extremely clearly going for heavily individualized targeting and hasn’t been shy about their intent to keep selected people in rather than jobs, which is illegal,” the union wrote.

The statement goes on to claim that management is betting on outsourcing to take on the workload of these fired team members — a decision that the union feels is “out-of-touch.”

The letter then says Don't Nod employees have been “living on the edge, in uncertainty and anxiety” for the last two years, to the point where six workplace accidents occurred this year and an inquiry was recently launched into a “serious and immediate danger.” It also alleges that management “refused to let those who would be willing to leave earlier go through a voluntary leave plan,” saying they “do not care about the damage it deals to employees’ health.”

The statement ends on a striking note; a government agency that represents employees is set to make its ruling on November 3. After that, management will have 21 days to decide on a plan. If this plan is accepted by the government agency, it’s possible that employees could “get their firing letters on November 25.”

“If it were to be rejected however, management would have to go back to the drawing board and improvise because, as you might have gathered, planning for contingencies isn’t their forte,” the letter concludes.

This is the latest news to surface regarding Don’t Nod’s dire financial straits after it was warned by auditors in a financial report that it could run out of cash as early as November. Its latest game, Aphelion , was released earlier this year to middling reviews, and given this recent union tell-all, its next project could be in peril.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .
